description: The command catalog (D-052, ADR-0002). Every function of LogReq is one command here. CLI, API, MCP server and app are generated from this file; schemas/generated/ is derived and checked in CI. Changing this file is a needs-human change.

commands.name: workspace.init
commands.summary: Create a workspace with the standard model in an existing folder.

path.description: Existing folder; must not contain logreq-workspace.yaml or the metamodel file.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: workspace.status
commands.summary: Repositories of the workspace, which are available, where the metamodel comes from, read-only state.

readOnly.description: LogReq cannot write the repository folder itself (read-only file system or no write permission). Reading works as usual and the workspace stays writable; writes into this repository are refused with file.read-only (SR-018 AK2). Rights on the Git server are not visible here (D-016, D-024). Only for available repositories; left out where the operating system cannot tell (Windows).

commands.name: workspace.check
commands.summary: Check the whole workspace against the metamodel: files, required and unknown properties, missing targets, cycles, duplicate IDs, outdated relations. CLI exits 1 on findings.

changedFiles.description: Only these files and their targets (not implemented yet, SR-092).

changedSince.description: Git revision; only files changed since then and their targets (SR-025 AK4) (not implemented yet, SR-092).

severity.description: Lowest severity of the problems shown; does not change ok or the exit code.

ok.description: False when the workspace has a finding of severity warning or error, shown or not (CLI exit code 1, ADR-0009).

durationMs.description: Time the check took in milliseconds. Not given yet: it differs between calls, and the cross-access test compares outputs (SR-080 AK2).

commands.name: metamodel.get
commands.summary: The effective metamodel: types with inherited properties, properties, relation kinds, statuses, meanings.

types.description: The types with inheritance resolved (SR-012), in metamodel order.

meanings.description: Every built-in meaning of metamodel.schema.json (`meaning` of types, properties and relation kinds) -> the keys whose own definition declares it, in metamodel order; empty if unassigned (SR-013 AK3). In a valid metamodel a type or property meaning has at most one key, a relation meaning any number. Types that inherit a meaning, or repeat the one they inherit, are not listed; `types` shows their effective `meaning`.

commands.name: element.create
commands.summary: Create an element with a new random UUID. Only title, text and required properties are needed; empty required properties give a hint (SR-064). New elements always get the initial status of the metamodel (D-030).

folder.description: Folder relative to the repository; default from the type.

commands.name: element.get
commands.summary: One element with text, properties, relations, version (and on request its date), hints, and which variants replace or exclude it.

versionDate.description: Also give the date of the version (`versionDate`, D-013, ADR-0005), read from the Git history. Without it no git runs and `versionDate` is left out, so opening an element stays fast (SR-082 AK3); the app asks for the date in a second call.

repository.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: the workspace name of its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (for example one copy of a file whose UUID another file shares, SR-088; #255). Only the elements ref names count; when none of them lies there, the error is ref.unknown with them as details.candidates.

file.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: its file, relative to its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (#255). Give repository too when the same path is in several repositories; when several elements are still left, the error is ref.ambiguous with them.

element.description: Text, properties, version and, with the input `versionDate`, its date (`versionDate`, D-013, ADR-0005: the committer date in UTC of the newest commit that started this version; null for content no commit has and when Git cannot tell, including a git call that timed out; left out without the input), the own relations, the successors of a superseded element (SR-072 AK3), the hints of the element (none while the metamodel is not valid; also `variant.superseded-in-validity`, SR-040 AK3, and `metamodel.meaning-unassigned` when no property has the meaning title) and `readOnly`, always given (unknown type, invalid metamodel or a repository folder that cannot be written). Later stages add the other incoming relations, and `verification` and `validation`. The variants that replace or exclude the element (SR-046, stage 5) have no field in the schema yet; they come with that stage.

commands.name: element.resolve
commands.summary: Resolve a reference from another tool (UUID or short ID, optional version) and tell whether the version is current.

version.description: The version the reference stores (D-013); optional. A version of another normal form than the one the tool computes (n1) is refused with input.invalid (ADR-0005).

versionDate.description: Also give the date of the current version (`versionDate`, D-013, ADR-0005), read from the Git history, as element.get does with the same input. Without it no git runs and `versionDate` is left out.

repository.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: the workspace name of its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (for example one copy of a file whose UUID another file shares, SR-088; #255). Only the elements ref names count; when none of them lies there, the error is ref.unknown with them as details.candidates.

file.description: Which of the elements ref names is meant: its file, relative to its repository, as details.candidates of ref.ambiguous give it (#255). Give repository too when the same path is in several repositories; when several elements are still left, the error is ref.ambiguous with them.

element.description: The element as element.get shows it, with title, text, status and current version (SR-060 AK1) and, with the input `versionDate`, the date of that version (as element.get gives it; left out without the input). An unknown reference is the error ref.unknown, one that fits several elements ref.ambiguous with details.candidates (AK3). A short ID whose prefix fits no element stays ref.unknown, never another element; when its tail fits exactly one element of another type, details.candidates names that element and the message asks whether its short ID was meant (prefix may be outdated, #275).

current.description: Whether the given version is the element's current version, computed from its file as it is now (SR-060 AK2); null when no version was given.

commands.name: element.list
commands.summary: Elements of a selection, sorted; optionally as derivation tree.

commands.name: element.update
commands.summary: Change title, text or properties of one element. Unknown properties are kept; status changes only via element.setStatus.

affected.description: The number of directly affected elements (SR-024 AK2): the distinct elements other than this one whose files hold a relation or an inline reference to it, the elements at distance 1 of `trace.affected`. Counted only when the save changed the version (the content, D-013); 0 when only the title or properties that do not count to the version changed, or nothing changed (SR-024 AK3).

commands.name: element.setStatus
commands.summary: Set the status of elements on explicit request of the caller. The only command besides element.supersede that changes a status; no command changes a status on its own (D-030, SR-087).

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: element.supersede
commands.summary: Supersede an element: set an invalid status and optionally let a successor replace it (relation with meaning replacement, written into the successor's file). There is no delete (D-045).

relation.description: Relation kind with meaning replacement to write from the successor; needed only when more than one fits the types and the successor does not already have the relation under exactly one of them.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: element.bulkUpdate
commands.summary: Set, add to or remove a property for all elements of a selection. Without `confirm` only previews.

commands.name: element.addAttachment
commands.summary: Copy an image next to the element file and return the Markdown to insert; the image counts to the version (SR-065 AK2).

commands.name: relation.options
commands.summary: Relation kinds and target types the metamodel allows for an element (SR-067).

commands.name: relation.add
commands.summary: Add a relation; stores target UUID and current version, plus the title only within the same repository.

commands.name: relation.remove
commands.summary: Remove a relation from the source file.

repository.description: Only relations into this repository (workspace name); a relation that names none points into the source's repository (D-058). Names the one meant when a UUID has relations into several repositories.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: trace.chain
commands.summary: Chain up to the top parents and down to evidence, with depth, gaps and cycles.

nodes.description: Every element of the chain once per direction, at its shortest depth (SR-022 AK1, AK2): the root first, then the parents level by level, then the children level by level. An element reached again (a diamond, a cycle) is not repeated; its edge is in `edges` (SR-022 AK4). In a view, only the elements that apply in it (SR-040); the root always. An element is named by its UUID and `repository` (D-058); two files of one repository with the same UUID (SR-088) are two nodes, told apart only by `file`, and edges and gaps name both the same way. A chain can be large (in a workspace of 50,000 elements and 200,000 relations up to about 42,000 nodes and 36 MB of JSON): a client that shows it step by step asks with `maxDepth` 1 and asks again below an element that is not `expanded`.

depth.description: Steps from the root: 0 for the root, 1 for its parents or children, and so on.

direction.description: `up` for a parent (and its parents), `down` for a child (and its children); left out for the root.

expanded.description: Its parents or children were looked at; false only at `maxDepth`, where the chain was cut.

edges.description: Every derivation relation the chain followed, from the child that stores it (`source`) to its parent (`target`, ADR-0004): the upward ones, then the downward ones, in the order they were followed.

sourceRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `source`.

targetRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `target`.

kind.description: Key of the relation kind with the meaning `derivation` (SR-013).

cyclic.description: Both ends lie in one cycle of derivations (SR-022 AK4).

gaps.description: The gaps of the downward chain (SR-022 AK3), in the order of `nodes`: `no-child` for a need without a child, `no-evidence` for a requirement without a child and without evidence. Only for elements whose children were looked at (`expanded`). Evidence records come in stage 4 (SR-028): until then every requirement without a child is `no-evidence`.

repository.description: Workspace name of the repository of the element with the gap.

unresolved.description: Derivation relations the chain could not follow (SR-006 AK1, SR-088, SR-089): upwards a parent that is not available, downwards a child whose relation points at a UUID several files of the repository share. The other end is shown by its short ID only when it is not available (prefix `UNKNOWN` when its repository is not on this machine). A parent whose `id` is no UUID is not listed (the value-kind check reports it, SR-085); in a repository that is not here it still makes the chain `incomplete`.

from.description: The element of the chain whose parents or children were looked at.

fromRepository.description: Workspace name of the repository of `from`.

id.description: The other end: the parent the relation names (up), the child that stores it (down).

targetState.description: As in `data-export.schema.json#/$defs/relation`; downwards always `ambiguous` (the element the child points at).

problems.description: Hints: `trace.cycle` once per cycle of derivations in the chain, naming its elements (SR-022 AK4); `metamodel.meaning-unassigned` when no type has the meaning `need` or `requirement`, so those gaps cannot be found (SR-013 AK3).

commands.name: trace.related
commands.summary: All children of a set of parents, or all parents of a set of requirements, each once, optionally up to a depth; one page at a time, total counts all.

limit.description: Elements of the page; total counts all.

offset.description: Elements skipped before the page, in the order of the list (by distance from the selection).

commands.name: trace.affected
commands.summary: Elements affected by a change of one element, with path and distance.

affected.description: The page of `limit` affected elements from `offset` (`total` counts all). The affected elements: every element that has a relation or an inline reference to the element, directly or through the chain (SR-024 AK1), each once at its shortest distance, breadth first, the element itself never. Distance 1: every element whose file holds a relation (any relation kind or relation-valued property) or an inline reference to it. From there onward along the derivation chain (meaning `derivation`, SR-013) and inline references that point at an affected element.

distance.description: Steps from the element: 1 when this element's file points at it directly.

path.description: The way: the element asked for first, this element last, each element in between that points at the one before it; each named by UUID and repository (D-058).

via.description: How this element points at the one before it on the path: a relation stored under `key` (a relation kind or a relation-valued property), or an inline reference in its text.

total.description: The number of all affected elements; `affected` holds the page of `limit` from `offset`.

records.description: The evidence records of an older version of the element (SR-024 AK4): records whose `version` is not its current one. Evidence records are read from stage 4 on (SR-028); until then the list is empty.

incomplete.description: True while a repository of the workspace file is not on this machine: elements there may point at the element (SR-006 AK2).

commands.name: hint.list
commands.summary: Open hints of the workspace, filterable by kind, type, package or variant.

commands.name: hint.confirm
commands.summary: Confirm hints: writes the current target version into the relation and nothing else (D-042).

commands.name: element.search
commands.summary: Full-text search over title, text, properties and IDs, typo tolerant, within a view or filter.

commands.name: filter.list
commands.summary: Saved filters of the workspace.

commands.name: filter.save
commands.summary: Save a named filter as YAML in the repository.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: evidence.list
commands.summary: Evidence records of an element with version, item, date, result, evidence location and baselines that contain the version.

commands.name: evidence.record
commands.summary: Write a manual verification or validation record; ID and current version are filled in.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: evidence.enrichJunit
commands.summary: Add UUID, version, item and date to every test case of a JUnit XML file that names a short ID. CLI exits 1 on unknown IDs.

commands.name: evidence.status
commands.summary: Verification and validation status of a selection per view, including indirect verification and missing children.

commands.name: evidence.coverage
commands.summary: Coverage of a selection per level: how many have children, how many have evidence; with the element lists.

commands.name: evidence.degree
commands.summary: Verification degree of a selection: share verified and count per status.

commands.name: data.export
commands.summary: Data of the current state as JSON for external evaluation.

commands.name: data.store
commands.summary: Write the data of the current state to a folder, file name contains the commit.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: variant.diff
commands.summary: What a variant adds, replaces and excludes compared to the core.

commands.name: variant.exclude
commands.summary: Exclude core requirements for a variant; written into the variant file only.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: baseline.create
commands.summary: Write a baseline file for a selection. Refused while selected elements have uncommitted changes. Never commits.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: baseline.list
commands.summary: Baseline files of the workspace.

commands.name: baseline.get
commands.summary: Elements of a baseline with their version then, marked changed, added or superseded since; optional evidence status per version.

commands.name: baseline.compare
commands.summary: The Git command and commits that show the difference of an element since a baseline (SR-051 AK3). Read only.

commands.name: reqif.analyze
commands.summary: Read a ReqIF file: types and attributes without mapping, and for a repeated delivery the new, changed and dropped requirements. Writes nothing.

commands.name: reqif.import
commands.summary: Import a ReqIF 1.2 file with a mapping; updates existing elements by IDENTIFIER, records origin, reports losses.

commands.name: reqif.saveMapping
commands.summary: Save or change the mapping of a source to the own metamodel.

items.description: Written file, relative to the workspace root.

commands.name: reqif.export
commands.summary: Export a selection or a saved export profile as ReqIF 1.2; IDENTIFIER is the UUID, or the source IDENTIFIER for statements.
